items.followUp: Write any two roles of enzymes in industry.

rubric.why: Enzymes help digest food by breaking it into simpler substances.
rubric.description: State the role of enzymes in digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying digestion as a use of enzymes.

rubric.why: Enzymes are used in detergents to help remove stains.
rubric.description: Name a second use of enzymes, such as their use in detergents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid use other than digestion.

modelAnswer: Enzymes help in digestion by breaking down food into simpler substances.
Enzymes are used in industrial detergents to help remove stains.

items.followUp: Differentiate between intracellular and extracellular digestion.

rubric.why: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cells in which they are produced.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating their action inside cells.

rubric.why: Extracellular enzymes are released from cells and act outside them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating their action outside cells or stating that they are released from cells.

modelAnswer: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cells in which they are produced.
Extracellular enzymes are released from cells and act outside them.

accept: no carbon to carbon double bonds
rubric.why: Saturated fatty acids have carbon atoms joined only by single bonds.
rubric.description: State the type of bonds between carbon atoms in saturated fatty acids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the carbon chain has single bonds and no carbon-to-carbon double bonds.

accept: maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms
rubric.why: A chain with no carbon-to-carbon double bonds holds the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.
rubric.description: State that saturated fatty acids contain the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-hydrogen feature.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have carbon atoms joined only by single bonds, with no carbon to carbon double bonds.
Their carbon chains therefore carry the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.

items.followUp: Explain the cellular and organ levels of biological organization.

rubric.why: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules.
rubric.description: Explain how molecules form at the molecular level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms combine or form molecules.

rubric.why: Molecules are organized into cell structures such as organelles.
rubric.description: Describe the organization of molecules into cell structures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking molecules to organelles.

rubric.why: A tissue consists of similar cells.
rubric.description: Identify the cellular composition of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a tissue is made up of similar cells.

rubric.why: The cells in a tissue work together to perform a particular function.
rubric.description: State what the cells of a tissue do together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared-function idea.

modelAnswer: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules such as water, proteins and lipids.
These molecules combine and are organized into cell structures called organelles.
A tissue is a group of similar cells, often with intercellular material, working together.
The cells of a tissue perform a particular function.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of the nucleus, with a labelled diagram.

rubric.why: A ribosome consists of a large and a small subunit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both subunits are correctly identified.

rubric.why: Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying RNA and protein as components.

rubric.why: Ribosomes do not have a surrounding membrane.
rubric.description: State that ribosomes lack a surrounding membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the non-membranous feature.

rubric.why: The main function of ribosomes is protein synthesis.
The diagram should show and label both subunits and the mRNA strand.
rubric.description: Draw a labelled ribosome diagram showing its subunits and mRNA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear diagram with the large subunit, small subunit and mRNA labelled.

modelAnswer: A ribosome is a small cell structure made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
It has no surrounding membrane and consists of a large subunit and a small subunit.
The two subunits come together during protein synthesis; ribosomes may be free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
